C1-irr-alignment.title: Alignment map is keyed on primary labels but tested against alternate labels — the reconciliation step is a no-op
C1-irr-alignment.impl_detail: In compute_coincidence (lines 217–222), alignment_map is built as alignment_map[primary_cat] = alternate_cat — keyed by primary label. The lookup at line 244 tests 'if cat_b in alignment_map', where cat_b is an alternate label. Because alternate labels never appear as keys in a primary-keyed dict, the branch at line 245 never fires; cat_b_aligned always equals the original cat_b. The same inversio
C1-irr-alignment.suggested_fix: In compute_coincidence (line 222), swap key/value: alignment_map[alternate_cat] = primary_cat. In compute_irr (line 705), swap: alignment_map[entry.get('alternate')] = entry.get('primary'). This ensures that when cat_b (an alternate label) is looked up, it is remapped to its corresponding primary label before coincidence counting.

C2-irr-independence.title: Independent researcher is same model and system prompt in a different session — correlated by construction
C2-irr-independence.impl_detail: SKILL.md lines 47–49: 'The alternate agent is a fresh subagent invocation — same agent file (mpi-analyst for per-transcript stages), different session context. It should produce its analysis independently, without seeing the primary analysis.' Independence rests solely on session isolation. Same model weights, same system prompt, same zero-shot strategy are used for both raters. compute_irr (irr.p
C2-irr-independence.suggested_fix: Either (a) require a different model for the alternate agent and enforce this via a manifest check; or (b) prominently caveat in SKILL.md and the IRR record output that the independence guarantee is session-context only (intra-model consistency, not inter-rater reliability). Structural isolation blocking the alternate agent from reading analyses/ would strengthen the session-isolation claim.

C3-global-synchronic-wiring.suggested_fix: Update SKILL.md line 13 to reference the actual artifact pattern: `analyses/event<E>-cat-<C>-gidu<G>-generic_synchronic.isu_second_level_grouping.md` for all events/categories relevant to the current `gidu<G>-cat-<C>` scope. C3-global-synchronic-wiring.suggested_fix: Replace SKILL.md line 18 'Write `analyses/global-synchronic.md`.' with the per-scope form: 'Write `analyses/gidu<G>-cat-<C>-global_synchronic.{json,md,prompt.json}` for the current scope.' This aligns the task description with the closure table and the agent persistence contract.

C3-global-synchronic-wiring.impl_detail: `_validate_global_synchronic` (lines 274–283) requires only `["generic_idu", "iv_category", "isus"]` at the payload level. `_validate_isu` (lines 122–129) requires `["isu_name", "criteria", "confidence", "flag_for_review", "utterance_refs", "isu_second_level_of_abstraction"]`. C3-global-synchronic-wiring.suggested_fix: Add `source_event` (or `event`) as a required field on each ISU object in `_validate_global_synchronic` (analogous to how `_validate_generic_synchronic_isu_second_level` requires `event` at the payload level). This would make event attribution machine-enforceable and auditable without a join.

C6-generic-synchronic-grouping.title: ISU grouping flattens across generic IDU boundaries — contradicts manual's within-IDU grouping rule
C6-generic-synchronic-grouping.impl_detail: Lines 93–100: 'ISUs are grouped by experiential similarity regardless of which IDU group they came from. Synchronic outputs nest ISUs inside isu_groups (one group per IDU); when comparing across participants, flatten all ISUs from all IDU groups and group them by semantic similarity.' The instruction explicitly dissolves the generic-IDU grouping boundary the manual requires.
C6-generic-synchronic-grouping.suggested_fix: Revise the 'ISU grouping rule' in mpi-cross-analyst.md to direct the LLM to group ISUs strictly within the target generic IDU, not across all IDU groups. The correct cross-IDU synthesis step is Global Synchronic Analysis, not Generic Synchronic Analysis.

Include it in the markdown output template.

C8-small-fidelity.title: Out-of-range IV score accepted silently by header regex
C8-small-fidelity.impl_detail: Line 89: `^Participant (\d+),?\s+Suggestion (\d+)(?:\s+\w+)*\s*\(Scored (\d+)/5\)` — the score capture group is `(\d+)` which accepts any non-negative integer. No downstream validation enforces score ∈ {0,1,2,3,4,5}. _mpi_schemas.py contains no score-range check. A header `Participant 1, Suggestion 1 (Scored 7/5)` would be parsed without error; the score 7 falls outside all defined category bounda
C8-small-fidelity.suggested_fix: After parsing the score integer, add a validation step: if score < 0 or score > 5, emit `ERROR: <filename>: score out of range. Expected 0–5, got <score>` and skip the file (consistent with the existing invalid-header error pattern in SKILL.md lines 97-99).

C8-small-fidelity.title: No warning when participant count falls outside the manual's 6-12 adequacy guidance
C8-small-fidelity.impl_detail: Lines 169-228 (the full Steps section): init scans all transcripts, builds participant entries, and reports the result table (lines 200-208), but at no point checks whether the total participant count per event falls within the 6-12 range or emits any advisory message. The schema in _mpi_schemas.py also has no participant-count validation.
C8-small-fidelity.suggested_fix: At the end of init (after building the participant table), emit a one-line advisory if any event_group has fewer than 6 or more than 12 participant transcripts, e.g.: 'Advisory: event1 has 4 participants; Guest et al. (2006) suggest 6-12 for adequate data saturation.'

C8-small-fidelity.title: Question removal not implemented in normalize step
C8-small-fidelity.impl_detail: The normalize step (lines 36–44) lists only: strip BOM, validate header, normalise whitespace, normalise speaker label capitalisation, remove CRLF. No question-removal logic exists. The Validation rules section (lines 19–44) and the Steps section (lines 62–69) contain no instruction to remove interviewer questions whose answers stand alone.
C8-small-fidelity.suggested_fix: Add a content-editing step to the normalize substep (or as a separate sub-substep) that identifies interviewer utterances (Kevin Sheldrake: lines) where the immediately following participant utterance is self-sufficient without the question, flags them for removal or human review, and optionally removes them with a diff recorded in transcripts/diff/.

C8-small-fidelity.suggested_fix: For criteria_grouping, make idu_name and moment optional (or accept a placeholder like 'TBD'). Only enforce idu_name/moment as required fields in the idu_naming_ordering validator. This would make the schema progression reflect the manual's intended sequencing.

C8-small-fidelity.impl_detail: mpi-analyst.md diachronic rules (lines 25–55) contain no mention of temporal linkage phrases or the instruction that utterances before/after a linking phrase should receive different criteria. Rule 2 (lines 26–29) directs grouping by 'shared experiential content' with criteria following 'The utterances talk about [X].' Rule 4 (lines 32–33) states 'When uncertain, prefer fewer IDUs' — which pushes
C8-small-fidelity.suggested_fix: Add a step to mpi-analyst.md diachronic rules instructing the analyst to scan for temporal linkage phrases as boundary signals, and to assign different criteria to utterances before versus after each such phrase.
